subject: EU data sovereignty, retention & deletion — technical and contract next steps

Subject: Data residency & retention clarifications for Acme EU account

Hi Soojin / Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move to procurement, legal has a few specific questions around EU-only processing and evidence for Schrems II / SCCs controls. High-level asks below — can you confirm which of these we can sign off on as-is and which will need contract language or tech changes?

- Will customer data for the Acme EU tenant be processed and stored only within the EU (data-plane, backups, logs)?
- Do you provide SCC-addendum wording we can attach to the DPA?
- How do you handle deletion requests: what APIs, time-to-delete, backups, and certificate/reporting can you provide?
- Are audit logs / behavior logs (traces, network logs) exported outside EU by default?
- Key management: do you support customer-managed KMS keys in an EU KMS?

We captured the questions in the attached PDF (Acme_SCC_questions_v1.pdf). Can we get a short written response and a pointer to the contract language? Procurement will need the doc for review.

Best,
Sven
Privacy & Compliance — Acme EU

Sven — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Neha (sales) so we can align contract + procurement. High-level answers first; Marcus will follow up with the technical specifics.

Summary answers (short):
- EU-only processing: Yes — for the Acme EU tenant we can ensure data-plane processing and primary storage remain in EU regions. We perform control-plane operations from our control plane (hosted) but customer data storage can be constrained to EU-only clusters per our Private/ Dedicated configuration.
- SCCs/DPA language: We have an SCC addendum and a standard DPA that references SCCs; Marissa will propose redlines for anything specific to Acme.
- Deletion: We expose deletion APIs and can provide deletion certification artifacts (export + deletion log). Marcus will detail retention windows and backup behavior.
- Logs: Application-level logs and customer data logs remain in-region by default for Dedicated/Private. Some telemetry for platform health (anonymized) may cross regions unless you opt into EU-only telemetry — Marcus will confirm.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys and can integrate with an EU KMS (bring-your-own-key).

Attachments: redwood-eu-processing-summary.pdf (high-level doc).

Next steps:
1) Marcus to send a tech note describing delete lifecycle and backup snapshots (by EOD tomorrow).
2) Marissa to send SCC addendum / DPA redline for procurement.
3) Neha to coordinate a short (30m) call with procurement & privacy.

I'll schedule the call once we have the technical note and the DPA draft.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai, Sven Müller <sven.mueller@acme-eu.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Data residency & retention clarifications for Acme EU account

Hi all — technical follow-up as promised. Long but intended to be prescriptive.

1) EU-only processing and storage
- For a Dedicated/Private deployment we provision compute and object storage exclusively in the selected EU region (e.g., eu-west-1). All models, KV caches, and token logs for the tenant are stored on those clusters.
- Control plane (orchestration) traffic is authenticated and limited; no customer content is written to the control-plane DB in the US. We can provide network diagrams and configuration snapshots on the call.

2) Backups and snapshots
- Backups are taken as incremental snapshots; for EU-only tenants snapshots are stored in the same EU region.
- Retention: default snapshot retention is 90 days, configurable down to 0 for customers who require immediate discard. Snapshots older than retention are purged by an automated job.

3) Deletion workflow (how to demonstrate deletion)
- API: DELETE /v1/customers/{tenant_id}/data — marks tenant for deletion and triggers purge pipeline.
- Purge pipeline: deletes primary storage, evicts KV cache, removes indices. Backups are queued for secure wipe.
- Time-to-delete SLA: primary data wipe completes within 7 days in normal cases; backups removed within 30 days unless a longer retention window is contractually required.
- Evidence: we can provide an audit bundle containing (a) deletion request ID, (b) snapshot purge logs, (c) S3 object-delete manifests for the tenant, and (d) an engineer-signed confirmation PDF.

4) Logs / telemetry
- Customer content logs (requests & model outputs) are stored in-region and are subject to the same retention policy as customer data.
- Platform telemetry (anonymised metrics / health) is aggregated and may be processed outside EU by default; we offer an EU-only telemetry option that keeps metrics within the EU and can be enabled for enterprise tenants.

5) Key management
- We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS; customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported. Keys can be provisioned in an EU region and referenced by the tenant for encrypting storage volumes and snapshots.

6) SCCs and cross-border risk
- We will provide our SCC addendum and a summary of transfer-impact-assessment controls: encryption of data-at-rest, no plaintext export from EU clusters, access controls, and logging. Marissa will provide the legal summary and proposed contract inserts.

Action items (tech):
- REDWOOD-ENG-1209: generate deletion audit bundle template for legal (owner: Marcus) — target 2026-02-20 EOD.
- REDWOOD-SEC-413: document EU-only telemetry configuration (owner: infra-security) — target 2026-02-25.

Attachment: marcus-deletion-api-spec.txt (small spec + example manifests).

Let me know if you want a scrubbed sample audit bundle for procurement to review.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
